key_insight: A learned patient world model can support multiple ICU policy simulations without rebuilding question-specific patient-state models.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can reuse a frozen clinical model while reconfiguring ICU resources, queues, and scenario mappings to evaluate operational policies.
method: Train a neural patient-trajectory model on longitudinal MIMIC-IV EHRs.
Freeze the model and connect time-queryable predictions to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues.
Use scenario-specific mappings to simulate bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer capacity.
evidence_signal: The model matched Markov and semi-Markov comparators on aggregate occupancy and directional policy responses, reproduced replay-based policy gains, and captured a history-dependent 24-hour recovery contrast of −6.4 versus −6.7 observed percentage points.
watch_item: Simulation agreement does not establish real-world policy effects; deployment requires external validation and checks of scenario-mapping assumptions.
paper_title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care
